topPRs.title: bailiff: add service to the monorepo
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## What

Imports the bailiff service (Go) into this monorepo and registers it in `.github/images.json`, so the monorepo builds and publishes the bailiff image. Source moved from the standalone bailiff repository.

## Change

- New `bailiff/` service directory, lifted from the standalone repo (Dockerfile unchanged, built with the service directory as context).
- `.github/images.json`: new `bailiff` entry (`context: bailiff`, `dockerfile: Dockerfile`, `paths: bailiff/**`).

## Verification

- `docker build ./bailiff` succeeds locally (image ~93MB), confirming the Dockerfile + context resolve correctly from the new location.
- `images.json` validated as well-formed JSON.

topPRs.title: chore: bump vulnerable dependencies to remediate CVEs (Go, yarn, poetry)
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Reduce dependency CVEs flagged by the Wiz scan by bumping vulnerable source dependencies to at least their fixed versions across all Go modules, the `replica-healthcheck` yarn workspace, and the `op-conductor-ops` poetry project.

The dominant fix is `golang.org/x/crypto` -> v0.52.0+ across every Go module, which alone addresses the bulk of the findings, plus `golang.org/x/net` -> v0.55.0+.

## Go modules

| Module | Package | Old -> New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cci-stats | jackc/pgx/v5 | v5.7.1 -> v5.9.2 |
| cci-stats | golang.org/x/crypto | v0.28.0 -> v0.52.0 |
| op-conductor-mon | golang.org/x/crypto | v0.38.0 -> v0.52.0 |
| op-conductor-mon | golang.org/x/net | v0.40.0 -> v0.55.0 |
| op-signer | consensys/gnark-crypto | v0.18.0 -> v0.18.1 |
| op-signer | go.opentelemetry.io/otel | v1.36.0 -> v1.41.0 |
| op-signer | golang.org/x/crypto | v0.41.0 -> v0.52.0 |
| op-signer | golang.org/x/net | v0.43.0 -> v0.55.0 |
| op-signer | google.golang.org/grpc | v1.74.2 -> v1.79.3 |
| op-txproxy | golang-jwt/jwt/v4 | v4.5.1 -> v4.5.2 |
| op-txproxy | golang.org/x/crypto | v0.26.0 -> v0.52.0 |
| op-ufm | golang.org/x/crypto | v0.23.0 -> v0.54.0 |
| op-ufm | golang.org/x/net | v0.23.0 -> v0.57.0 |
| op-ufm | golang.org/x/oauth2 | v0.16.0 -> v0.36.0 |
| op-ufm | google.golang.org/grpc | v1.56.3 -> v1.82.0 |
| peer-mgmt-service | golang.org/x/crypto | v0.31.0 -> v0.52.0 |
| peer-mgmt-service | golang.org/x/net | v0.25.0 -> v0.55.0 |
| proxyd | go.opentelemetry.io/otel | v1.40.0 -> v1.41.0 |
| proxyd | golang.org/x/crypto | v0.46.0 -> v0.52.0 |
| proxyd | golang.org/x/net | v0.48.0 -> v0.55.0 |

CVEs addressed (Go): CVE-2024-45337, CVE-2025-22868/22869/22870/22872, CVE-2025-47913/47914, CVE-2025-58181, CVE-2026-25680, CVE-2026-39821, CVE-2026-39827..39835, CVE-2026-42508, CVE-2026-46595..46598 (x/crypto, x/net, x/oauth2); CVE-2026-33186 (grpc); CVE-2026-29181 (otel); CVE-2026-33815/33816/41889 (pgx/v5); GHSA-fj2x-735w-74vq (gnark-crypto); CVE-2025-30204 (golang-jwt).

Each module was verified with `go build ./...` (or `go vet ./...` where the pre-existing local linker limitation applies).

## yarn (replica-healthcheck)

Added a `resolutions` block forcing patched transitive versions: `@babel/core` 7.29.6, `@eslint/plugin-kit` 0.3.4, `ajv` 6.14.0, `bn.js` 5.2.3, `brace-expansion` 2.0.3, `diff` 5.2.2, `flatted` 3.4.2, `glob` 10.5.0, `linkify-it` 5.0.1, `lodash` 4.18.0, `markdown-it` 14.2.0, `morgan` 1.11.0, `on-headers` 1.1.0, `path-to-regexp` 0.1.13, `picomatch` 2.3.2, `postcss` 8.5.10, `qs` 6.15.2, `serialize-javascript` 7.0.5, `tmp` 0.2.6, `underscore` 1.13.8, `uuid` 11.1.1, `ws` 8.21.0.

Verified with `yarn install`, `yarn build` (tsc) and `yarn lint:check` (eslint) all green.

## poetry (op-conductor-ops)

- urllib3 2.6.3 -> 2.7.0
- requests 2.32.4 -> 2.34.2
- idna 3.7 -> 3.18
- pygments 2.18.0 -> 2.20.0
- black 25.1.0 -> 26.5.1 (constraint widened to `>=25.1.0`)

`cli.py` reformatted so `black --check .` (run in CI) passes. Imports verified.

## Not bumped (with reason)

- `consensys/gnark-crypto` in op-conductor-mon, op-txproxy, op-ufm, peer-mgmt-service: bumping to v0.18.1 breaks the transitively pinned `crate-crypto/go-kzg-4844` (it references gnark APIs removed in newer releases). These modules use an older op-geth that still depends on go-kzg-4844; upgrading op-geth is out of scope. Left at v0.12.1.
- `quic-go/quic-go` and `quic-go/webtransport-go` in peer-mgmt-service: bumping breaks the pinned `libp2p@v0.32.0`, which imports the `quic-go/quic-go/logging` package removed in newer quic-go. Requires a libp2p/op-node upgrade, out of scope.
- js-yaml, minimatch, yaml (yarn): these appear at multiple incompatible major versions in the tree; yarn v1 resolutions cannot scope a fix per-major (range-keyed resolutions are unsupported) and forcing a single major would break API consumers. Left unchanged.
- `pion/dtls/v2`: no fixed version is available for CVE-2026-26014, so nothing to bump.

topPRs.title: chore(docker): migrate infra Dockerfiles to Chainguard wolfi-base
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Description

Standardises all `infra` service Dockerfiles on **Chainguard `wolfi-base`**, replacing the `dhi.io/*` and remaining stock base images. `op-conductor-ops` already used `chainguard/wolfi-base`, so this brings the rest of the repo in line and removes the DHI-registry auth dependency (Chainguard `wolfi-base` is public).

Part of the cloud-security Dockerfile-hardening effort (cloud-security#243, follows #234).

## Changes

Builder and runtime stages now use `chainguard/wolfi-base:latest`. Wolfi package mappings:

| Service | Before (builder / runtime) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| cci-stats, op-signer, op-txproxy, peer-mgmt-service | `dhi.io/golang-dev` / `dhi.io/alpine-base` | `alpine-sdk` → `build-base` |
| op-conductor-mon | `dhi.io/golang:1.24-dev` / `dhi.io/alpine-base` | added explicit toolchain install |
| op-ufm, proxyd | (CGO) `dhi.io/golang-dev` / `dhi.io/alpine-base` | `gcc musl-dev linux-headers` → `build-base` |
| replica-healthcheck | `node:23-alpine` / `dhi.io/node:22` | `nodejs-24` + `yarn` (build), `nodejs-24` + `npm` (runtime) |

Other decisions:
- Go toolchain installed via the versioned `go-1.26` Wolfi package.
- Wolfi is glibc, not musl, so CGO builds (op-ufm, proxyd) drop the musl-specific dev packages and use `build-base`; the glibc runtime is `wolfi-base`.
- `replica-healthcheck`: both stages moved to **nodejs-24** (active LTS). The original mixed a node-23 builder with a node-22 runtime, and the repo `.nvmrc` pinned the now-EOL `v23.9.0`. Standardised on node 24 and bumped `.nvmrc` to `v24.18.0` (node 23 is EOL; node 24 is LTS and is the version the Wolfi `npm` package supports, so there is no npm/node mismatch warning).
- `proxyd`: `ARG BUILDER_IMAGE`/`RUNTIME_IMAGE` defaults and the `Makefile` docker targets repointed to Chainguard.
- `op-conductor-ops` unchanged (already Chainguard).

## Testing

- All 8 images build on the CI matrix (`build-images.yaml`), both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.
- Built and run locally (arm64): every image starts and reaches its own app-level config check — no exec/linkage/missing-runtime failures.
  - Go services (op-signer, op-txproxy, op-ufm, peer-mgmt-service, proxyd) also keep their in-build `--help` / exit-code smoke tests, which exercise the binary in the Wolfi runtime during the build.
  - cci-stats and op-conductor-mon reach their config checks; replica-healthcheck runs `npm run start` on node 24 into the app (needs runtime RPC config), with no npm warning.

## Notes

Not a base-package CVE claim on its own; this is the incremental Dockerfile-hardening path alongside apko/melange (not a replacement). Image size / package-count / Grype deltas to be captured once CI publishes the new images.
